body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for The Ghostlight Express: 8 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: The letter in the mailbags (Silas), the doctor's medical bag (Cordelia) and the handbill in the circus car (Delphine) are those companions' own scenes: do not mention them. Do not name the creatures in the cars or say what is wrong with the train. Nobody knows the train will crash.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Rook + Tobin + Silas (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, tobin_hayward, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party is on Barrow Hill about to board the Ghostlight Express. Nothing has gone wrong yet.
  In front of them: Barrow Hill: A burying hill at the end of a lane, a ring of standing stones on its crown, and a shelf on its east side where a black train waits on rails of mist. A low hill wears a ring of standing stones, and its west slope is all leaning headstones under an old yew hung with paper lanterns. Past the stones the ground levels into a shelf where a black engine sits on rails made of mist, it... Parts of it: The lychgate; The burying ground; The standing stones; The shelf; The hollow. Things to see: The lychgate; Carved turnip lanterns; An old yew hung with paper lanterns; Leaning headstones; Iron grave-markers; The ring of standing stones; The fallen stone; A tumbled drystone wall; A scarecrow among the graves. People here: The Vagrant.
EXCHANGE 2: Delphine + Lucan + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, lucan_houndstooth, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The train is running through the dark. The party has just come into the lounge car. Lucan's hound is only ever called Dreadfang.
  In front of them: The Lounge Car: Ebony and gold, burgundy velvet, a long black bar, and a smoking singer at the window. Understated luxury: ebony walls inlaid with gold lines, burgundy velvet chairs in quiet corners, frosted sconces and a long black bar with a mirrored back. Parts of it: The bar; The seating; The window seat. Things to see: The bar; The landscape paintings; Landscape paintings; Burgundy velvet chairs; An empty whiskey bottle; A jug marked XxX. People here: Phillip Druskenvald; Adela Druskenvald; The Songstress.
EXCHANGE 3: Tobin + Delphine (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The train is running. The party has come into the dining car.
  In front of them: The Dining Car: Six four-seat booths down each side, white cloths, brass-rimmed menus, and a big empty half-booth at the front. Booths under white cloths line both walls beneath orange paper bunting. At the front end an eight-seat half-booth is laid with a spotless cloth and nobody has ever sat at it. Parts of it: The booths; The big booth. Things to see: A booth; Brass-rimmed menu cards; The empty half-booth. People here: Mrs. Calloway.
EXCHANGE 4: Rook + Delphine (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The train is running. The party has come into the mail car.
  In front of them: The Mail Car: Pigeonholes of letters from the dead to the living and back, a sorting bench, canvas mailbags, and an old sailor hauling them about. Two long walls of pigeonholes: letters from the dead on the north wall, letters from the living on the south. An old sailor hauls canvas mailbags from one pile to another. Parts of it: The living-to-dead shelves; The dead-to-living shelves; The sorting bench. Things to see: Letters from the living to the dead; Letters from the dead to the living; A bright pink envelope; Canvas mailbags; The sorting bench; A letter on the bench. People here: The Mariner.
EXCHANGE 5: Rook + Lucan (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The train is running. The party has come into the baggage car. Lucan's hound is only ever called Dreadfang.
  In front of them: The Baggage Car: Heaps of dusty luggage, the Druskenvalds' new trunks, and a snoring tiger of green flame behind a stack at the front. Luggage is piled to the ceiling in rough stacks with narrow ways between them. Near the rear door the Druskenvalds' new leather trunks glimmer; somewhere at the front something large is snoring. Parts of it: The front stacks; The rear stacks; The tiger's den; Where the tiger sleeps. Things to see: The Druskenvalds' trunks; A steamer trunk; Abandoned luggage; A discarded medical bag; The sleeping tiger; The iron ring on its tail. People here: The Jailbird.
EXCHANGE 6: Rook + Cordelia (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The train is running. The party has come into the circus car.
  In front of them: The Circus Car: A travelling show's car: rusted cages, striped crates, banners of clowns, and a jester hanging from a trapeze. Rusted animal cages line the north wall, one with its door bent open and its straw scorched. Red-and-white crates, banners of laughing clowns and, overhead, a trapeze swinging with a jester hanging from it by her knees. Parts of it: The cages; The stage end. Things to see: The rusted cages; An open cage; A ring of keys on a hook; Red-and-white crates; Carnival banners; A poster for the Festival of Fools; A marionette chest; The trapeze. People here: The Harlequin.
EXCHANGE 7: Tobin + Lucan (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party has reached the Tender, the fuel car at the front of the train. Lucan's hound is only ever called Dreadfang.
  In front of them: The Tender: An ironclad fuel car: a black tank full of drifting soul coal, pipes along the walls, and a furnace in the front wall. A cast-iron tank with a round glass porthole fills the middle of the car, full of soul coal drifting like banked embers. Pipes run over the walls to a furnace in the front wall. There is no way forward. Parts of it: The vestibule; The tender. Things to see: The porthole; Pipes over the walls and ceiling; The firebox; The Tender's door.
EXCHANGE 8: Tobin + Cordelia (speaker ids: tobin_hayward, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The Ghostlight Express has crashed. The party stands at the wreck, in a wood in a bowl of land.
  In front of them: The Ghostlight Wreckage: An ancient oak wood in a bowl of land, a crash groove gouged through it, and a locomotive pinned on its side by black roots under a crescent moon with a crone's face. A groove forty yards across has been ploughed through the oaks, and the carriages lie scattered like dropped cards. On a rise in the east the engine lies on its side, black roots holding it, and above the broken canopy hangs a moo... Parts of it: The clearing; The engine's bank; The oaks; The tree line. Things to see: The roots; The crash grooves; The scattered cars; A car in the oak; Mossy boulders; A glint in the roots; A glint by the groove; A glint under a boulder; A pool of soul-mist. People here: The Vagrant; Phillip Druskenvald; Adela Druskenvald; The Ghostlight Locomotive.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 8 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 8, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY rook_coldwake: That tumbled drystone wall is a textbook subsidence hazard, Tobin, and nobody's reset the fallen standing stone in a century. Poor parish upkeep, start to finish.
SAY tobin_hayward: Never mind the masonry, Rook, look at the scarecrow planted by the yew. Sloppy stitching round the collar, and they've stuffed him with damp meadow hay that's already gone to mould.
SAY silas_vane: Forget the straw man, friend, we are about to board a locomotive parked on rails of actual fog. Tell me where the house keeps the brakes on a cloud.
SAY rook_coldwake: Schedule's posted by the lychgate, Silas, so the track bed is the ferryman's jurisdiction. Just mind the turf by those iron markers as we cross.
SAY tobin_hayward: At least they carved proper turnip lanterns for the walk up. Gives a man a warm feeling in the collarbone.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY delphine_ravelle: Ebony panelling, burgundy velvet, and a Songstress at the glass who knows how to hold a room. Now this is proper headliner billing, darlings.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: The upholstery is admirable, Delphine, though Dreadfang is staring rather fixedly at that jug marked with three crosses behind the bar. I suspect the vintage lacks breeding.
SAY cordelia_skein: Never mind the spirits, Lucan, observe how the frosted sconces flatter theDruskenvalds' complexion. I would love to assay whatever preservative keeps them so charmingly poised.
SAY delphine_ravelle: He says the landscape paintings are moving when we blink, and he doesn't even have eyes. Do keep your glass vials away from the velvet, Cordelia, one spill ruins the nap.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: If you please, let us take a corner booth before the smoke thickens. It plays havoc with a hunter's nose.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY delphine_ravelle: Six booths a side, crisp white linen, and orange bunting that looks like a third-rate harvest tent. Someone couldn't decide between a banquet and a barn dance, Tobin.
SAY tobin_hayward: The cloth on that big eight-seat booth at the front hasn't got a crease or a crumb on it, Delphine. Whole table laid out for company that never showed.
SAY delphine_ravelle: A reserved box with no curtain call, darling, and brass-rimmed menus nobody has ever opened. Even Mrs. Calloway looks like she's waiting on a cue that missed the train.
SAY tobin_hayward: Good linen shouldn't sit idle while the dust settles on the plates. Makes my stitches itch just looking at an empty row.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY rook_coldwake: Sound filing system in here, Delphine: north pigeonholes for the dead, south for the living. Would save our parish clerk three weeks of sorting every winter.
SAY delphine_ravelle: It is all dreadfully drab canvas, Rook, except for that bright pink envelope wedged in the north rack. Who sends boudoir stationery from the grave?
SAY rook_coldwake: So long as the postage is squared on the docket, the colour of the paper isn't the watch's concern. Look at the Mariner hauling those sacks without a trolley.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Well, if anyone writes to me from the cheap seats beyond the veil, they had better use gilt edging. I have a reputation to keep.
SAY rook_coldwake: Nobody's writing to me from either wall, lass. Best we leave the sorting bench clear.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY rook_coldwake: Piling steamer trunks to the ceiling with barely a foot of clearance is a gross violation of gangway zoning, Lucan. One sharp bend and the whole stack comes down.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, Rook, there is a tiger of green flame asleep behind the front luggage, and it wears an iron ring upon its tail. Prime specimen, though its breathing is remarkably loud.
SAY rook_coldwake: Open flame in an unventilated baggage car, and right beside the Druskenvalds' new leather trunks. Did nobody on this crew read the shift log?
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Dreadfang has flattened his ears at the scent, if you please, so let us step lightly past the Jailbird. I would rather not grade a flaming feline in a narrow aisle.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY rook_coldwake: Rusted cages with the bars bent outward and scorched straw on the floorboards, Cordelia. Someone let the stock loose and didn't even log the damage.
SAY cordelia_skein: Look at the thermal scoring on the iron, Rook, the specimen must have generated extraordinary internal heat before vacating. And the Harlequin overhead hasn't dropped a single beat on her trapeze.
SAY rook_coldwake: Hanging by the knees in a moving carriage is unruly behaviour, circus or not. And don't go clicking your eyes at that marionette chest, we've no warrant to pry.
SAY cordelia_skein: You have no poetry in your thorax, darling, though I grant you the ring of keys on that hook is a laughable security measure. Even a mindless beast could lift it.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep two paces back from that firebox, Lucan, the heat coming off the front wall is curling the straw in my cuffs. One loose spark from those pipes and I am kindling.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Step behind my coat, Tobin, if you please, the cast-iron tank is quite secure. Though I confess the soul coal drifting behind that glass porthole has a most unsettling posture.
SAY tobin_hayward: Looks like banked embers, only cold and grey round the edges, like rot in an old stump. Nothing ought to burn without leaving clean ash for the soil.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Dreadfang will not look through the glass at all, and there is no door forward from this vestibule. Whatever feeds this furnace, friends, it was never meant to be hunted.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY tobin_hayward: Forty yards of good ancient oak ploughed up like a turnip furrow, and black roots pinning the engine on its side. That taproot didn't grow by accident, Cordelia, it reached up and caught us.
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology in the wood, Tobin, the vascular fibres have constricted around the iron boiler like a muscular spasm. And do check your left cuff, darling, your little primrose survived the impact.
SAY tobin_hayward: So it did, and not a petal torn, while the carriages are scattered over the moss like dropped kindling. Look at that pool of soul-mist leaking into the hollow.
SAY cordelia_skein: My vials are intact, thank goodness, though that crone-faced moon overhead is doing strange things to the ambient humours. Do hold still while I brush the oak bark from your seam.
